items.headline: Mountain View weighs legal action against fire truck makers
items.summary: The City Council met in closed session to discuss a potential case involving several major fire apparatus manufacturers, including Pierce, Oshkosh, REV Group, Rosenbauer America, Golden State Fire Apparatus, and the industry's Fire Apparatus Manufacturers' Association. The council also discussed appointing a new City Attorney.

items.headline: TIAA approved for three illuminated wall signs on El Camino Real
items.summary: Architectural review was approved for three illuminated wall signs for TIAA at 2875 El Camino Real, signaling the financial firm's branded presence at that address.

items.headline: Massage Envy gets approval for new LED signage on El Camino Real
items.summary: Two new LED channel letter wall signs were approved for Massage Envy at 2515 El Camino Real.

items.headline: Campbell to split $335,000 resurfacing cost with San Jose
items.summary: The council approved a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, capped at $335,000, to fund a joint resurfacing project.

items.headline: Council reviewed red light camera traffic safety program
items.summary: City Council received a presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program and considered authorizing next steps for the city.

items.headline: Council briefed on condition of Milpitas Community Center
items.summary: City Council received a presentation on the current condition of the Milpitas Community Center and discussed how to proceed.
